articles.title: Pokémon ETBs are Surprisingly Easy to Get Hold of Right Now on Amazon
articles.summary: Amazon has quietly restocked high-demand Pokémon TCG Elite Trainer Boxes below secondary market prices, including hard-to-find Pokémon Center Exclusives and new releases.
body: If you've been looking around the shelves over the last few months, then you've almost definitely realised that Elite Trainer Boxes (ETBs) are as hot as a Torkoal using Sunny Day at the moment, and they're flying off the shelves!

The intense popularity of the Mega Evolution expansion, the surge of nostalgia ahead of the franchise's 30th Anniversary, and the continuous pressure from secondary-market scalpers (thanks, Logan Paul ) have all contributed to the high demand for sealed ETBs. Will the retail frenzy ever end? One day, hopefully, but the realistic answer is most likely no, not for a while.

Yet, despite the odds, Amazon has quietly restocked a surprising range of high-profile ETBs at decent prices. I've tracked down the best deals I can find on Amazon US and UK right now; everything from the most recent summer releases to the hard-to-find Pokémon Center Exclusives to save you from your fights with the bots.

When you tally up the individual retail cost of buying nine standalone booster packs alongside official sleeves, dice, and custom storage, an ETB is pretty decent value. If you can get it at a decent price, that is. Fortunately, that’s where we come in!
points: Amazon has quietly restocked high-demand Pokémon TCG Elite Trainer Boxes below secondary market prices, including hard-to-find Pokémon Center Exclusives and new releases.

articles.title: How Elgato Can Level Up Your WFH Setup - From Lighting, To Audio, And More
articles.summary: Working from home is a common practice for many of us these days, and while that’s very welcome indeed for a number of reasons, it does mean productivity nerds like myself get to have fun with new accessories to take our home office setup to another level.
body: Enter Elgato, the company perhaps best known for the Stream Deck, and an array of products that can help you look better, sound better, and even get more done.
We’ve already written in depth about the Stream Deck lineup (not to be confused with Valve’s excellent handheld PC).
The more recent Stream Deck + adds a touch strip and dials, and is ideal for editing music or video, while the Stream Deck Neo is super small but includes touch points, 8 keys, and an infobar, too.

If you thought the Stream Deck was just for becoming a content creator, think again. Whether you’re on PC or Mac, I recommend looking into them - they’re able to help you get your work done more swiftly. Plus, I’d be lying if I said it wasn’t just very fun to have more buttons to press, especially with the sheer amount of customization available.

body: Even Dungeons & Dragons, a tabletop staple that became synonymous with 1980s nerd culture, has enjoyed a major resurgence in recent years.

But nostalgia doesn’t always guarantee commercial success. One particularly expensive action-fantasy revival tried to bring an unmistakable hero of the 1980s back to theaters this summer. Audiences didn’t exactly rush out to see it — but it's been a hit since arriving on streaming.

After struggling during its theatrical run, Masters of the Universe, director Travis Knight’s $175 million live-action revival of He-Man, has become a major hit on Prime Video, ranking among the platform’s biggest movies globally, according to FlixPatrol.
Masters of the Universe takes the basic He-Man mythology and gives it a modern blockbuster makeover.

articles.title: GTA 6 Leak and Wolverine Rage Are Symptoms of Gaming's Summer of Hate
articles.summary: A lot bad news and a lack of major game releases has fed a poisonous atmosphere in gaming; Gamescom and the September releases can't come soon enough
body: Man, it's been a rough summer, but I promise you, it's nearly over.

It has always been like this. For decades, the game industry has more or less shut down — or reduced itself to a small hum of subsistence — between the noisy previews of E3/Summer Game Fest in early June, and the noisy previews of Gamescom in late August. People go on vacation, players spend more time outside, and there are few big games released. Then Gamescom fires the starting gun on the busiest release period of the year.

It's never been quite like this, though. This year, releases slowed down but the news cycle didn't. We had the Xbox layoffs, Sony killed physical games. Everyone was hot and angry. The gulf between the number of exciting new games to play and talk about and the number of enraging topics to consume the discourse just kept growing. The algorithms must be fed, after all, even if it's only with bitter gruel. This week, gaming's summer stumbled to an exhausted climax with the Grand Theft Auto 6 leaks, which started out fun and, like everything else, quickly turned awful.
points: A lot bad news and a lack of major game releases has fed a poisonous atmosphere in gaming; Gamescom and the September releases can't come soon enough

articles.title: Silent Hill: Townfall's new gameplay trailer quietly confirms how long its PS5 exclusivity will last
articles.summary: A new Silent Hill: Townfall gameplay trailer has offered up over 18 minutes of first-look footage while also quietly confirming exactly how long the game's PlayStation 5 exclusivity will last.
body: The extended trailer follows protagonist Simon Ordell as he explores the fog-shrouded Shorefront region of the fictional Scottish island of St. Amelia, picking through houses and apartments, gathering items, and eventually running into some of the horrors lurking in the mist.

The trailer's closing fine print held the more notable reveal, though. Alongside reiterating that Townfall is a PS5 console exclusive, a caption confirmed: "Also available on PC. Not available on other consoles until at least 6 months after release date".
That's not a confirmed Xbox Series X/S or Nintendo Switch 2 release, of course, but it does give a rough window for when one could happen: from around March 2027 onward.

Developed by Screen Burn Interactive (the studio FKA No Code) and published by Konami and Annapurna Interactive, Townfall is also notable as the first mainline Silent Hill game to be played entirely in first-person. It's set to release on 24th September on PC and PS5.

articles.title: Is this the end of the GTA 6 leaks? Take-Two's legal crusade appears to shut down the hubs behind them
articles.summary: Take-Two's legal offensive against the source of the ongoing GTA 6 leaks appears to have claimed its first scalp: the CyberLeek website, one of the group's main hubs, has gone offline.
body: The group's Telegram channel has also gone dark, now displaying only the message "This channel is unavailable due to copyright infringement".

The disappearance comes just days after Take-Two filed subpoenas targeting Microsoft and Discord, seeking information that could identify whoever is behind the CyberLeek persona. Both companies have until 4th September to hand over relevant account data.

The leaks – which have been popping up all week – have been substantive, showing co-protagonist Jason tearing around Vice City in a supercar and shooting the word "leek" into a wall, suggesting some kind of playable access to GTA 6.

As Bertie summarised for us at the time, CyberLeek has maintained that it's doing the leaks in the name of gamers' rights, but behind it is a shady cryptocurrency scheme involving a $CYBERLEEK meme coin the group wants people to buy (and thereby increase the value of) to vote for new video leaks. Ostensibly, this is being done to fund "a secret project", but as Polygon reported, there's evidence to suggest dodgy-seeming personal gain.

articles.title: 30 Years Ago, One Console and Two Games Changed My Life
articles.summary: Switchboard is Polygon's weekly newsletter for all things Nintendo, sent on Thursdays and published on the site on Saturdays. You can subscribe here.
body: This Sunday, Aug. 23, is the 35th anniversary of the release of the Super Nintendo Entertainment System in North America. We'll be celebrating the console with a series of articles on Polygon over the weekend, so I'm not going to dive too deep into its brilliance, or the generational hot streak that it inspired in Nintendo's in-house studios, here. But I thought I'd share a personal perspective on it.

I grew up with the video games of the 1980s home computer scene in the U.K.; my foundational texts were the likes of Manic Miner, the early works of Rare (then called Ultimate Play the Game), and the homebrew aesthetic of solo coders like Jeff Minter. I largely missed the 16-bit era in my teens because my family couldn't afford a new computer or console. I remember yearning for an Atari ST and coveting my best friend's Sega Genesis (called the Mega Drive over here). I drifted away from games and got into movies. I had basically no contact with Nintendo at all.

articles.title: Double Fine confirms it owns all its games' IP and publishing rights after Xbox split
articles.summary: Double Fine has confirmed it owns – or will shortly own – the intellectual property and publishing rights to every game it made during its seven years under Xbox following the studio's split from Microsoft earlier this year.
body: CEO Tim Schafer confirmed the news on Kinda Funny Games (thanks, IGN ), fielding a fan question about whether buying Double Fine's back catalogue - including Psychonauts 2, Keeper, and Kiln - actually puts money in the studio's pocket.
"I saw a question there: 'Do you guys make the money on games?'" Schafer said. "The transfer of the IP came back to us, and we get the publishing rights back to all our games."
That said, "some of [the games]" remain with Xbox for the time being, but Schafer explained that "it just takes a while for it to all process".
"If you're curious, buying any of our games helps support the studio," he emphasised. "We can turn that money into revenue that helps us extend that runway."

articles.title: 7 Years Later, One 'Vinland Saga' Line Remains Anime’s Greatest Lesson About Violence
articles.summary: Vinland Saga initially looks like the kind of anime built around everything its story eventually comes to reject. It has vikings, bloody raids, brutal battles, revenge, and a young protagonist who spends years consumed by the desire to kill the man responsible for his father's death.
body: “Listen to me, Thorfinn. You have no enemies. No one has any enemies. There is no one in this world that you should hurt.”

It’s a powerful sentiment, but Vinland Saga understands it’s an almost impossible one to live by. Thors isn't simply telling Thorfinn to be a better person. He's asking him to reject one of the most basic assumptions of the world around him: that violence is inevitable, that enemies are real, and that strength means having the ability to hurt someone else. For a Viking warrior, that philosophy is almost incomprehensible. For Thorfinn, it becomes even harder to accept because his entire childhood up to this point has been shaped by violence.

These clashing ideals are what make Vinland Saga so compelling. It doesn't present pacifism as an easy moral victory. Thorfinn doesn't hear his father's words and instantly becomes a peaceful person. He spends years trapped in the cycle of violence that Thors wanted him to escape. Even after he finally begins to understand what his father meant, choosing peace remains incredibly difficult.
points: Vinland Saga initially looks like the kind of anime built around everything its story eventually comes to reject.
It has vikings, bloody raids, brutal battles, revenge, and a young protagonist who spends years consumed by the desire to kill the man responsible for his father's death.

body: There's so much - so much - invisible labour in making video games, but every now and then you catch something and it makes you think about the person who must have made that. One corner of your base in Star Wars: Zero Company has a little empty chair with an empty bottle next to it, facing out of one of its windows.It's not a pointed, deliberate discovery or anything, just the way the furniture in that area's been arranged. But someone chose to put that chair facing that way and put a bottle next to it, to make me think, if I happened to be paying attention to my surroundings for once, that some crew member must sit there from time to time and gaze at the stars.

articles.title: The Sinking City 2 Review
articles.summary: The Sinking City 2 feels inescapably like off-brand Resident Evil, but it's a praiseworthy imitation of its main inspirations wrapped in the Cthulhu mythos.
body: It was impossible for me to play The Sinking City 2 for more than 15 minutes without coming to the obvious realization that this is Resident Evil in a fedora. That might sound dismissive, but I really enjoy the recent Resident Evil games, so comparing Frogwares' Lovecraftian survival horror sequel to some of the best of them – which feels especially similar to 2019's Resident Evil 2 remake – is much more of a compliment than a put-down. What sets it apart begins with its unique, rich, 1920s New England setting flush with loving detail that instills a strong sense of personality over the top of the mechanics it so clearly imitates.

You play as Calvin Rafferty, a likeable occultist waking up to an apocalyptic flood set to wipe out the entire city of Arkham, Massachusetts in 1929. He's definitely a little bit of a pulp fiction stock character: hard-chinned, two-fisted, and foolishly brave. But there are layers to him that rise to the surface here and there. Similar to the Resident Evil comparison, likening him to the classic heroes of the genre is not really an insult.
points: The Sinking City 2 feels inescapably like off-brand Resident Evil, but it's a praiseworthy imitation of its main inspirations wrapped in the Cthulhu mythos.

articles.title: Dishonored was a last-ditch effort by Arkane Studios after years of fruitless contract work, according to the game's co-creator: 'I think we had four months of money left'
articles.summary: Former Arkane Austin head Harvey Smith recently announced his new studio, Black Pony Immersive. As the name suggests will be dedicated to making immersive sims in the tradition of Deus Ex and System Shock.
body: As it turns out, however, this isn't the first time that Smith has bet the house on an immersive sim and come up trumps. That's exactly what happened with Dishonored —the game that cemented Arkane's reputation as the new guardian of this particular strand of RPG.

Speaking to The Game Business, Smith revealed that Dishonored was a ride or die project, a way out of a mire of fruitless contract work for other developers. "People would come tell us 'Man, to keep the business alive, you better take some contracts. You need to be working on whatever you can get.' And for a while we tried that, even though it felt wrong."

Despite some promising projects like a cancelled Half-Life 2 episode, Smith's fears proved justified: "There was a point in time when Arkane was about to go under. I think we had four months of money left. We were working on Boom Blox with EA. We were pitching to Ubisoft. We had a couple of guys on a zombie shooter. We were farming people out left and right. We were on nine projects at once."
points: Former Arkane Austin head Harvey Smith recently announced his new studio, Black Pony Immersive.
As the name suggests will be dedicated to making immersive sims in the tradition of Deus Ex and System Shock.

articles.title: 'Hoping for a Huge October Surprise, But Not Holding My Breath' — Arc Raiders Players Torn After Embark Delays Future Expeditions Until Early 2027
articles.summary: Embark Studios has announced that all future Arc Raiders Expeditions have been delayed until early 2027 as it aims to "return with major improvements" following community feedback.
body: The developer behind the early 2026 extraction shooter hit announced the change in its post-launch schedule in an update on the Arc Raiders website today. It came with confirmation that Expedition 5 will launch when the window opens September 8 and close September 29, but after that, the Rust Belt will be quieter than normal.

"We have been carefully reviewing your feedback on Expeditions," Embark's post said, "and while we've made ongoing improvements along the way, we've come to realize that some of the issues you've raised, like the tight departure windows, the reward structure, and accessibility for new players, need more than incremental fixes. They call for bigger changes."

"In order to address those concerns, we need to pause the Expeditions for a while. The fifth Expedition will be the last one until early 2027, when Expeditions will return with major improvements, tackling some of the biggest player pain points. So, if you’ve been on the fence about departing - now is the time! We will share more details on what those changes will look like in September."

articles.title: The latest cooperative craze is a physics-based fishing simulator where you can launch your catch into the air and no-scope it with a sniper rifle
articles.summary: As someone who grew up in the '90s and early '00s when cooperative games were scarce, I'm a big fan of this current era of cheap and cheerful experiences designed to play with your pals.
body: As such, I'm always interested to see what coop nonsense bubbles up to the surface of Steam's algorithm next, and it appears the catch of the day is How to Fish, a 1-4 player, physics- based fishing simulator where you subdue marine life in the most preposterous ways possible.

The premise sees you and your pals stranded on a barren, rocky islet after drunkenly crashing onto its shores. You start out surviving by picking clams off the rock, which offer meagre sustenance. But you can also sell the clams for cash (which you do in the traditional manner of shoving them into an old seadog's mouth) thus enabling you to buy a fishing rod and begin learning how to fish.

The fishing element of How to Fish is relatively simple. You cast your line, wait for something to take the bait, and reel it in. Where things get more interesting is in what happens after you've landed a catch. Fish and other sea-life don't just appear in your inventory: they will flop, scuttle or crawl around land until you've subdued them. Initially, you'll have naught but your fists to do this with, but over time, you can purchase knives, brass knuckles and even guns you can use to exact bloody vengeance on the ocean.
points: As someone who grew up in the '90s and early '00s when cooperative games were scarce, I'm a big fan of this current era of cheap and cheerful experiences designed to play with your pals.

videos.summary: Today, Game Science unveils a brand-new 15-minute gameplay trailer for Black Myth: Zhong Kui, the second title in the Black Myth series. The trailer offers a first look at the protagonist in combat, along with a glimpse of the story.
body: As the game is still in early development, all footage was captured in-game from a work-in-progress build running at a 21:9 aspect ratio. The final release may differ.

points: Today, Game Science unveils a brand-new 15-minute gameplay trailer for Black Myth: Zhong Kui, the second title in the Black Myth series.
